summary: A Center for Biological Diversity web page titled "12 Ways to Live More Sustainably" lists twelve everyday actions to reduce environmental footprint and leave room for wild animals and plants. Each action gets a short explanation covering shopping, plastic, diet, holidays, organic products, fashion, water, driving, home energy, boycotts, family planning, and political advocacy, with links to related campaigns and resources.
one_line: Twelve individual actions, from secondhand shopping to voting, that reduce environmental footprint and protect wildlife, published by the Center for Biological Diversity.
key_facts: At least 14 million tons of plastic ends up in the ocean annually, making up 80% of all marine debris.
In the United States nearly 40% of edible food goes to waste.
In December, Americans create 23% more waste than in other months of the year.
More than 2 billion pounds of pesticides are sold annually in the United States.
The number of new garments made per year has nearly doubled over the past 20 years.
Global consumption of fashion has increased by 400%.
The fast fashion industry is responsible for as much as 10% of global carbon emissions.
A tire that is 20% underinflated can increase a vehicle's fuel consumption by 10%.
Products made from animals on the endangered species list are illegal to buy, sell, import or trade in the United States.
The page notes that with more than 8 billion people in the world, human demands are pushing other species toward extinction.
Food is the single largest category of material thrown into municipal landfills.
The page recommends choosing an electricity supplier that generates at least half of its power from wind, solar and other clean sources.
The page recommends avoiding bluefin tuna by dining at restaurants that refuse to serve imperiled species.
Animal-based textiles like wool are linked to water pollution and widespread habitat loss from deforestation.
Xeriscaping uses native, drought-adapted plants that require less water and maintenance over time.
